Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NexGen Renewables Inc. Q4 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A, please press * then 1 on your telephone keypad to ask a question. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NexGen Renewables' results for the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2023. Joining me on today's call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Development Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Tom Hargrove, Chief Sustainability Officer; Raj Singh, Chief Operating Officer; Nina Keller, Chief Strategy Officer; and David Wong, Chief Risk Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. NexGen Renewables continues to demonstrate its leadership in the renewable energy sector, achieving a record-breaking performance in the fourth quarter. Our success is a testament to our unwavering commitment to innovation, sustainability, and operational excellence.

Today, I want to highlight eight key aspects of our performance. First, our revenue and earnings growth has accelerated dramatically. Second, construction progress across our pipeline remains ahead of schedule with firm commercial operation dates. Third, we've maintained disciplined debt levels and contained financing costs. Fourth, PPA pricing trends are strengthening alongside successful contract extensions. Fifth, tax equity and project-level financing have unlocked substantial capital efficiently. Sixth, significant market trends are propelling our growth. Seventh, capital recycling through asset sales is fueling reinvestment. And eighth, government incentives and subsidies have provided a powerful tailwind.

Let me start with the second aspect—construction progress and commercial operation dates—which remain a cornerstone of our growth story at NexGen Renewables. As a leader in utility-scale solar PV, onshore wind, and battery energy storage systems, our 12 GW development pipeline underscores our execution prowess amid the global clean energy boom. With the U.S. Inflation Reduction Act's PTC and ITC extensions fueling a 25% year-over-year increase in our construction backlog to $4.2 billion, we're on track to commission over 2.5 GW across our key regions this year and next.

Our flagship U.S. Southwest solar portfolio has leveraged the IRA's 30% domestic content bonus to accelerate builds. The 650 MW Desert Bloom Solar project in Riverside County, California—our largest single-site bifacial PV array using 600W+ TOPCon modules from LONGi and Nextracker single-axis trackers—is 92% complete on engineering, procurement, and construction. Civil works wrapped up in May, with module deliveries 100% on-site despite earlier Red Sea supply chain hiccups. We've poured 1.2 million cubic yards of concrete for foundations and achieved first power from a 50 MW test block last quarter. Commercial operations are locked in for Q4 2024, ahead of our original H1 2025 target, thanks to our strategic partnership with First Solar for thin-film modules on the back half. This positions us to capture California's NEM 3.0 dispatchable capacity mandates, with a 15-year PPA at $28/MWh from Southern California Edison already inked.

Moving east to Texas, ERCOT's load growth—projected at 10 GW annually through 2028—has been a tailwind. The 800 MW Lone Star Solar + 400 MWh BESS hybrid in West Texas is 78% EPC complete. Tracker installations are at 65%, with 85% of our 2.2 million JinkoSolar Tiger Neo N-type modules racked up. The integrated BESS, using Tesla Megapack 2XL units with 4-hour duration, hit factory acceptance testing last month and is now 40% installed. Interconnection with ERCOT's queue is fully approved under the new Generator Interconnection Reform, shaving six months off timelines. COD for the full hybrid is Q1 2025, with solar-only energization by year-end. This project's LCOE is modeling at $22/MWh, down 15% from our 2023 builds, driven by 25% higher module efficiency and AI-optimized O&M via our proprietary NexGenOS platform.

In the Midwest, wind remains resilient despite turbine lead times. Our 450 MW Prairie Winds Phase II in Oklahoma, featuring Vestas V150-6.0 MW platforms with 155-meter hubs for enhanced capacity factors above 45%, is 55% complete post-NTP in March. Foundation pours are done for 75 turbines, with erection at 20 units per month. Supply chain de-risking via U.S.-sourced nacelles under the IRA's advanced manufacturing credit has kept us on budget. COD slips to Q3 2025 from Q2 due to avian permitting tweaks with the USFWS, but we're mitigating with radar-based curtailment tech from IdentiFlight, achieving 99% uptime in pilots. Corporate offtakers like Meta, who signed a 200 MW slice at $35/MWh fixed, are thrilled with the hedge against natural gas volatility.

Internationally, we're expanding thoughtfully. In Australia, our 300 MW SunHub Solar farm in Queensland—partnered with SunPower for Maxeon 7 IBC modules—is 88% complete, with COD in Q4 2024 aligning with AEMO's 82% renewables target by 2030. Grid upgrades via Transgrid's $1.5 billion Energize program have fast-tracked us. And in Europe, under REPowerEU's €300 billion push, our 250 MW Spanish PV portfolio in Andalusia hit FID last week, with construction starting Q4 2024 for H2 2026 CODs. Auctions there yielded €22/MWh strikes, beating our internal $25/MWh hurdle.

Strategically, our pipeline conversion rate from shovel-ready to construction now stands at 65%, up from 52% two years ago, thanks to front-loading $500 million in interconnection deposits and hedging 70% of turbine/module costs via futures on the CME green energy curve. We're prioritizing hybrids—40% of our 5.2 GW under construction—to address duck curve challenges and unlock storage ITC adders up to 40%. Risks like interest rate sensitivity on our $2.8 billion project finance facilities are hedged 80% at SOFR +150 bps, and we're exploring yieldcos for post-COD monetization akin to Clearway's model.

In summary, with 3.8 GW expected to reach COD in FY24-25—delivering $1.1 billion in contracted revenue at 12-15% EBITDA margins—our execution de-risks the business while capitalizing on falling hardware costs, with solar modules down 20% YoY to $0.22/W, and policy tailwinds. We're not just building assets; we're shaping the grid of tomorrow.

Now, I'll hand the call over to Michael Chen to provide a detailed review of our financial results and expand on the other key aspects.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. Our financial performance in the fourth quarter was exceptional. Revenue reached $812 million, representing a 62% increase compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by significant project commissioning and increased energy production. Our gross margin expanded to 28.2%, reflecting improved operational efficiency and cost management. Operating expenses totaled $450 million, primarily due to investments in R&D and sales and marketing. Net income was $312 million for the full year, or $1.84 per share. We ended the quarter with $650 million in cash and cash equivalents. We are significantly raising our full-year guidance for revenue to $3.85 to $4.05 billion and earnings accordingly.

Let me dive deeper into the remaining aspects, starting with revenue and earnings growth analysis, which underscores NexGen's accelerating leadership in the clean tech transition. As a reminder, we define adjusted EBITDA to exclude one-time items like restructuring costs and non-cash stock compensation, providing the clearest view of our underlying operational performance.

Q4 revenue came in at $812 million, up 62% year-over-year from $502 million in Q4 2022, beating our guidance midpoint by 8%. Full-year revenue reached $2.91 billion, up 45% from $2.01 billion in FY 2022. This marks our seventh consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, driven by hyperscale project executions, favorable policy tailwinds, and our pivot toward high-margin energy storage and hybrid solutions.

By segment, our diversified portfolio delivered balanced growth. Solar EPC and module sales, 58% of FY23 revenue at $1.69 billion, surged 52% YoY, fueled by delivery of 4.2 GWdc across utility-scale projects. Key wins included our 1.2 GWdc SunForge portfolio in the U.S. Southwest, leveraging bifacial TOPCon modules with 23.5% efficiencies—outpacing competitors like First Solar's thin-film tech on a cost-per-watt basis. Wind, 24% of revenue or $698 million up 38% YoY, benefited from 1.8 GW of onshore turbine installations, including our co-developed 600 MW RidgeLine project in Texas with Siemens Gamesa, where we integrated proprietary digital twin software for 15% O&M cost reductions.

Energy Storage Systems, now 13% of revenue at $378 million—a 112% YoY jump—thanks to 2.5 GWh deployed in BESS projects. Our LFP-based containerized systems, with 95% round-trip efficiency and 10-year warranties, captured share in front-of-the-meter applications, including a landmark 850 MWh hybrid solar-plus-storage PPA with Southern California Edison. Services and O&M rounded out at 5% or $145 million, up 22% on recurring revenue from 12 GW under management.

Geographically, North America drove 65% of FY23 growth, with U.S. revenue at $1.72 billion, a 59% YoY increase, supercharged by $12 billion in backlog from the Inflation Reduction Act's PTC/ITC extensions and manufacturing credits. Our new 2 GW Texas gigafactory, qualifying for 45X advanced manufacturing PTCs, will add $300 million in domestic content revenue by FY25. Europe contributed 22% or $640 million up 35%, aligned with REPowerEU targets—we closed €450 million in auctions for 1.1 GW of bifacial solar-plus-storage in Spain and Germany, navigating permitting via streamlined FAST-41 processes. APAC, 13% or $378 million up 42%, saw strength in Australia's NEM market with 800 MWdc of floating solar, though China exposure remains under 5% due to localization; we're countering with JVs like our pact with Adani Green for 500 MWh storage in India.

On profitability, earnings growth outpaced revenue, reflecting operational leverage. Q4 adjusted EBITDA hit $182 million, up 110% YoY with margins expanding 590 basis points to 22.4%. Full-year adjusted EBITDA reached $612 million, up 78% from $344 million, at a 21.1% margin—up 450 bps from 16.6% in FY22 and approaching our 25% medium-term target. Gross margins improved due to scale efficiencies with fixed costs per MW down 18% at 92% fab utilization; supply chain optimization with polysilicon hedged at $0.22/W, 25% below spot, and ESS cell prices down 30% YoY; premium product mix with hybrids now 35% of backlog boosting margins 400 bps; and policy capture like $150 million in IRA transferability and EU CBAM premiums.

Free cash flow turned positive at $210 million, funding $450 million in FY24 capex without dilution. These results validate our "Hybrid Horizon" initiative: integrating solar/wind with 4-hour storage at under $50/MWh LCOE, undercutting gas peakers. We've secured 8.5 GW backlog at over 25% gross margins, 70% contracted through 2027 via investment-grade PPAs. Risks like ERCOT delays are mitigated by $200 million in liquidated damages and AI queue optimization.

For FY24, we guide revenue to $3.85–$4.05 billion (32–39% growth), adj. EBITDA $850–$900 million (39–47% growth, 22–22.5% margins), and EPS $2.45–$2.65, embedding 6 GW deployments, $1 billion IRA/ITC inflows, and first perovskite revenue.

Next, on debt levels and financing costs, which underpin our growth in utility-scale solar, offshore wind, and long-duration storage. Total gross debt stood at $2.75 billion end-Q4, up 8% YoY from $2.55 billion, driven by drawdowns on our $1.5 billion revolver for 800 MW BESS in California and Texas, backed by 15-year PPAs with PG&E and ERCOT entities. Net debt is $2.1 billion after $650 million cash, at 3.2x net debt-to-adjusted EBITDA—within 3.0x-4.0x target, down from 3.8x year-end 2023, thanks to $420 million quarterly operating cash flow from 5.5 GW operating portfolio.

Debt-to-equity is 0.65x, with $1.2 billion liquidity providing 18-month runway. Weighted average cost of debt is 4.1%, down 50 bps YoY via refinancing. 65% fixed-rate at 3.9% post-hedges. Highlights include $500 million green bonds at 3.75% maturing 2034, oversubscribed 4.2x for 300 MW Spanish solar.

In U.S., IRA transferability reduces spreads 20-30 bps via tax equity with US Bancorp. Europe refinanced €400 million at SOFR+125 bps equivalent. APAC at 4.8% offset by subsidies. 40% debt sustainability-linked, shaving 15 bps; 80% floating hedged to 2027 at 3.2%. Project finance non-recourse for 75% new builds, like $1.1 billion Texas BESS at 3.5% fixed, DSCR 1.8x year one.

Net debt peaks at $2.4 billion mid-2025 then delevers to 2.8x by 2026 on $1.5 billion FCF. Costs compress 20-30 bps via green sukuk and PFIC.

Turning to PPA pricing trends and contract extensions, key to backlog stability with PPAs covering 85% of 12 GW portfolio. PPA prices for solar-plus-storage up 15-20% YoY. U.S. Southwest now $32-38/MWh vs. $22-25 in Q3 2021. Hyperscalers doubled PPA appetite per LevelTen, favoring our 450 MW Desert Bloom at $35/MWh with BESS.

Supply constraints from interconnection delays push pricing. Europe EEG at €45-55/MWh up 10%; UK CfD offshore at £44/MWh. U.S. regional: CAISO $36/MWh, ERCOT $42/MWh hybrids. Australia AUD 55-65/MWh.

Extensions on 1.2 GW YTD added $1.4 billion backlog at 12% above original, like Texas Wind Ridge from $28 to $36/MWh with repowering and BESS, de-risked by IRA grants. Our PPA 2.0 Initiative with AI forecasting converts 70% discussions. Blended fixed with merchant collars capture spikes.

Expect +5-8% pricing 2025, 80% extension capture, supporting $2.8-3.1 billion FY25 revenue.

On tax equity financing and project-level financing, these fund our 5 GW pipeline at blended 5.2% cost. Tax equity, 35% of funding, swaps ITC/PTC for capital; IRA adders hit 50% ITC. Closed $850 million YTD, like $325 million Wells Fargo for 450 MW Arizona hybrid at 7.2% IRR. Transferability sells credits at 90-95 cents/dollar, speeding closings.

Project-level non-recourse debt 50-55% capex, $1.2 billion Q4 including $650 million green bonds for 600 MW California at SOFR+140 bps. Stacks 35/50/15 tax/debt/equity.

Enable $15 billion backlog at 1.8x net debt/EBITDA. Innovate with hybrids for ITC adders, premiums.

For FY25, $3-4 billion new financings.

Regarding significant market trends and their impact, global renewables hit $1.8 trillion investment, 510 GW additions 2024, solar 380 GW at $0.11/W modules. BESS LFP $90/kWh. Corporate PPAs 50 GW.

U.S. IRA $100 billion credits boost our 20 GW pipeline, 70% contracted $35/MWh, data centers key. Margins up to 28%.

Europe REPowerEU 600 GW solar goal, but delays; our 8 GW at 35% EBITDA.

APAC China 120 GW, India 40 GW; our 4 GW high-margin.

LATAM/MENA upside. Drove 28% revenue growth, BESS 35% mix, margins +400 bps.

Invest $500 million next-gen: perovskites, iron-air storage, H2. Guide $10-11 billion FY24 revenue.

On capital recycling and asset sale transactions, we've generated $2.8 billion cumulative since 2021 at 12.5% IRR. Q2 closed $650 million: 400 MW U.S. solar to Brookfield at 1.45x multiple, $480 million proceeds; 250 MW Spanish wind €150 million at 7.1% cap.

YTD $1.1 billion, delevering to 3.2x, liquidity $1.4 billion, IRR 13.2%. U.S. 65%, Europe up 40%. Evolving to H2 assets, 5 GW recyclables for $3-4 billion, 2 GW FY24 target. Funds 70% $5 billion capex.

Finally, the impact of government incentives and subsidies contributed $185 million to Q2 EBITDA, 28%. U.S. IRA 60%, $320 million ITC transfers on SunForge, $42 million 45X on gigafactory.

Europe 25%, EEG €65/MWh wind, UK CfD £44/MWh offshore. APAC India PLI 50%, Australia CIS.

Shifting to performance-linked, 65% pipeline hybrids under $25/MWh unsubsidized. $210 million Q2 monetized. Risks policy cliffs, hedged by merchant 30% EBITDA.

Project $1.2 billion through 2027, 18-20% FCF CAGR.

I'll now turn the call over to Lisa Patel to discuss our project development activities.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Michael. Our project development pipeline continues to grow rapidly, with 12 GW of projects under development across various renewable energy technologies. We are making excellent progress on securing land rights, obtaining permits, and negotiating power purchase agreements. We expect to bring a substantial number of new projects online in the coming quarters, further contributing to our revenue and profitability. We are also actively pursuing strategic acquisitions and partnerships to accelerate our growth.

Dr. Elena Vasquez, can you update us on our technological advancements?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Lisa. We are committed to driving innovation in the renewable energy sector. Our R&D efforts are focused on developing groundbreaking technologies that enhance the efficiency, reliability, and affordability of renewable energy systems. We have made significant breakthroughs in areas such as advanced solar panel technologies like perovskite tandems targeting 35% efficiencies, energy storage solutions including iron-air flow batteries for long-duration dispatch, and smart grid technologies with AI-driven curtailment and yield optimization. We believe that these technologies will revolutionize the energy landscape, supporting green hydrogen electrolyzers scaling to 1 GW and agrivoltaic dual-use for higher yields.

Next, Tom Hargrove will discuss our sustainability initiatives.

Tom Hargrove:
Thank you, Elena. Sustainability is deeply ingrained in our corporate culture, and we are committed to minimizing our environmental impact and contributing to a more sustainable future. We have established ambitious goals for reducing our carbon footprint through Scope 1/2 emissions cuts tied to sustainability-linked debt, improving energy efficiency via 92% round-trip BESS and recyclable turbines, and promoting responsible resource management with domestic content and low-soiling modules. We are also actively involved in community engagement, supporting local initiatives around our projects, and advancing green hydrogen and DAC retrofits eligible for 45Q credits.

Now, Raj Singh will provide operational highlights.

Raj Singh:
Thank you, Tom. Our operational performance remains exceptional. We are focused on optimizing our operations, improving efficiency, and ensuring the reliability of our renewable energy assets across 12 GW under management. We are implementing best-in-class practices in asset management with digital twins for 15% O&M savings, proactive maintenance using IdentiFlight and VerdantOS equivalents, and supply chain management hedging polysilicon and LFP cells. We are also investing heavily in training and development to ensure our employees have the skills for hybrid deployments and AI queue tools.

Nina Keller, can you provide an update on our strategic initiatives?

Nina Keller:
Thank you, Raj. We are focused on executing our long-term strategic plan, which includes expanding our presence in key markets like ERCOT, CAISO, Iberia, and APAC; diversifying our product offerings into hybrids (40% backlog), green H2, and CCUS; and strengthening partnerships with hyperscalers, Siemens Gamesa, LONGi, and yieldcos. We are also actively exploring new opportunities in emerging areas such as green hydrogen electrolyzers, long-duration storage, and offshore wind floats.

And finally, David Wong, can you address our risk management strategies?

David Wong:
Thank you, Nina. We have implemented robust risk management strategies to mitigate potential risks associated with our operations, including market risks from rate hikes hedged 80%, regulatory risks via FAST-41 and FERC 2023, and environmental risks with radar curtailment and avian tech. We are continuously monitoring and evaluating our risk profile—interconnection queues, supply chain via hedging, policy cliffs—and taking proactive steps like liquidated damages clauses and GridOptix forecasting to manage these effectively. Covenant headroom exceeds 200 bps.

I'll turn it back to Sarah for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you all. In conclusion, NexGen Renewables had a truly exceptional fourth quarter. We are confident that our strategic initiatives, our commitment to innovation, and our unwavering focus on sustainability will continue to drive long-term growth and success.

Operator, let's proceed with the Q&A session.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to register for a question, please press * then 1 on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from Jordan Lee with GreenCapital Partners. Please go ahead.

Jordan Lee:
What are your plans for investing in new technologies such as green hydrogen?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thanks for the question, Jordan. Green hydrogen is a key pillar of our innovation roadmap, aligning with EU Hydrogen Bank and U.S. 45V credits. We've allocated $150 million in capex for 100 MW PEM electrolyzer pilots integrated with solar hybrids, partnering with ITM Power for Rotterdam hub offtake. Our Texas 50 MW electrolyzer-solar bundle is in late development, targeting NEOM-style green ammonia. Expect first revenue 2026 at 15% IRR, scaling to 1 GW by 2027 via IPCEI funding, de-risked by LCOE under $2/kg with perovskites and long-duration storage. This diversifies beyond solar/wind/BESS while capturing $5.4 billion EU subsidies.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with EcoInvest Advisors. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
How are you managing the increasing competition in the renewable energy market?

Sarah Thompson:
Great question, Emily. Competition is intensifying, but our hybrid focus—35% backlog—differentiates us with dispatchable power at $22-28/MWh LCOE, undercutting peakers. We lead in execution with 65% shovel-ready conversion, AI queue optimization advancing 20 projects, and vertical integration in trackers/microinverters. Backlog 35 GW at 4.5x book-to-bill, 95% IG PPAs through 2027. Recycling $1.1 billion YTD funds M&A like our Enphase tuck-in, while IRA domestics boost margins 400 bps over pure-play solar peers. Diversified regions/geos mitigate China risks via JVs.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Marcus Hale with SustainFund. Please go ahead.

Marcus Hale:
Can you discuss the potential impact of climate change on your operations?

David Wong:
Certainly, Marcus. Climate change poses both risks and opportunities. Extreme weather could impact yields, but our P50/P90 DNV forecasts incorporate 8760-hour climate models, with soiling mitigation and radar tech ensuring 99% uptime. Resiliency via hybrids addresses duck curves/curtailment <5% in ERCOT/CAISO. Positively, load growth from heat domes boosts ancillary revenue—ERCOT spikes to $85/MWh. We're Scope 3-neutral via offtaker matching, with S&P ESG-linked debt kicking 15 bps savings after 25% renewables milestone. Insurance covers 80% assets, dynamic hedging GridOptix for volatility.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sophia Grant with RenewVest. Please go ahead.

Sophia Grant:
What are your expectations for the long-term profitability of your renewable energy projects?

Michael Chen:
Thanks, Sophia. Long-term profitability is robust, with FY24-25 CODs at 12-15% EBITDA margins on $1.1 billion revenue, scaling to 25% medium-term via scale (fixed costs -18%/MW) and mix (hybrids 400 bps lift). 8.5 GW backlog >25% gross margins, ROIC 15%+ per BNEF. Recycling at 13.2% IRR, FCF $1.5 billion annually delevering to 2.8x. Unsubsidized LCOE $25/MWh undercuts gas; extensions +12% pricing. FY25 revenue $2.8-3.1 billion, EPS CAGR 15-20% through decade, outpacing peers on solar-storage skew.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, there appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Sarah Thompson for any closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you all for your participation in today's call. We appreciate your continued support of NexGen Renewables. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
